reference: Chevrolet Corvette Z06 coupe (C8, MY2023 onward) - engineering reference only; the game car gets a fictional name
mainSpec: Base Z06 coupe (no Z07 package), US market, 1LZ-3LZ trims share the mechanical spec

tagLegend.F: manufacturer figure (GM/Chevrolet), possibly read through a mirror of GM data
tagLegend.P: published spec from a third party (spec database, magazine spec box, Wikipedia)
tagLegend.E: estimate; the note says how it was made

beliefCheck.belief: LT6, 5.5 L naturally aspirated DOHC flat-plane V8, 670 hp at 8,400 rpm, redline 8,600
beliefCheck.note: 670 hp (500 kW) at 8,400 rpm and 460 lb-ft (624 Nm) at 6,300 rpm are SAE J1349 US ratings. Some secondary spec pages wrongly print '6.2 L' or 'peak power at 8,600'. Export markets rate it 475 kW (646 PS) at 8,550 rpm.

beliefCheck.belief: Tremec 8-speed dual-clutch with a shorter final drive than the Stingray
beliefCheck.note: Tremec TR-9080 (GM M1L). Same eight ratios as the Stingray; final drive 5.56 vs 5.17 (Stingray Z51, eLSD) or 4.89 (Stingray base, mechanical LSD).

beliefCheck.belief: Use base Z06 as main spec, Z07 as variant
beliefCheck.note: Base Z06 = Michelin Pilot Sport 4S ZP, Brembo iron brakes, standard aero, Magnetic Ride. Z07 = Pilot Sport Cup 2 R ZP, carbon-ceramic brakes, high-downforce aero (734 lb at 186 mph), FE7 chassis, 189 mph top speed instead of 195.

trims.note: Trims are equipment levels; mechanical spec is shared.

value: Carbon Aero package (exposed or painted carbon)

assembly.value: Bowling Green Assembly, Kentucky, USA; LT6 engines hand-built in Bowling Green

productionCounts.note: As printed on Wikipedia; not cross-checked.

marketsUS.value: US and Canada: 670 hp (500 kW) at 8,400 rpm, 460 lb-ft (624 Nm) at 6,300 rpm, SAE J1349

marketsExport.value: Europe, UK, Japan, Australia, New Zealand: 475 kW (646 PS) at 8,550 rpm; 595 Nm at 6,300 rpm
marketsExport.note: Japanese catalogue lists 623 Nm (63.6 kgf m) instead of 595 Nm; the two export sources disagree. Lower rating presumably reflects export emissions hardware (not confirmed).

rightHandDrive.value: RHD built for UK, Japan, Australia, New Zealand

projectName.value: Gemini (design began 2014; first proof-of-concept engine Sept 2015)

layout.value: 90-degree V8, longitudinal, mid-mounted ahead of the transaxle

crankshaft.value: flat-plane (180-degree) forged steel crank, four-bolt mains, crank-mounted fluid damper, no balance shafts

displacementCalculated.note: Computed from published bore x stroke x 8 = 5,462.9 cc (333.4 cu in).

valvetrain.value: DOHC per bank, 4 valves per cylinder (32), finger followers on solid lifters with robot-selected shims, nested dual valve springs

camPhasing.value: electro-hydraulic VVT, about 55 deg intake and 25 deg exhaust authority; no variable lift

rodsPistons.value: forged titanium connecting rods, forged aluminium pistons with oil squirters

fuelSystem.value: direct injection, max 350 bar (5,076 psi); premium fuel

intake.value: two moulded-nylon plenums of 5.5 L each, one 87 mm electronic throttle body per plenum; three 'communicator' valves between the plenums (two work as a pair, one on its own schedule) tune Helmholtz resonance
intake.note: Motor1, citing SAE, says two valves stay closed until 2,000 rpm and the third opens at 5,800 rpm (S09). GM's torque chart shows steps near 3,000-3,500 rpm and 6,000-6,300 rpm, so treat the schedule as approximate.

lubrication.value: six-stage dry sump scavenging each crank bay; about 10 qt; 5W-50 dexos R oil
lubrication.note: Corvsport lists 8.0 qt oil capacity; Wikipedia 10 qt.

redline.note: Tachometer redline; shown in Chevrolet's reveal teaser.

revLimiter.note: Motor Authority: 8,600 rpm is the fuel shut-off point; at full throttle the gearbox completes the upshift at about 8,500 rpm.

limiterHysteresis.note: Not published. Typical hard fuel-cut bounce for a light DOHC engine.

idleRpm.note: Not published (gap). Warm idle estimated 850-1,000 rpm for a high-specific-output NA DOHC V8; reviewers call the idle 'ragged'. Cold-start flare estimated about 1,500 rpm.

launchControlRpm.note: Driver-adjustable launch rpm and allowed tyre slip (Corvette Blogger, Apr 2022, from a Chevrolet video). The Stingray's TR-9080 launch holds 3,500 rpm (S10).

engineInertia.note: Not published. Crank, rods share, damper and dual-clutch drum for a light flat-plane V8 (the V12 prototype uses 0.20).

firingOrder.note: Given by several firing-order references and a Corvette spec guide; not seen in a GM document.

cylinderNumbering.value: GM convention: odd cylinders 1-3-5-7 on the LEFT bank (driver's side of a left-hand-drive car; GM 'bank 1'), numbered front to rear; even cylinders 2-4-6-8 on the RIGHT bank. In the C8 the engine's front (accessory drive) faces forward toward the cabin, so cylinder 1 is the left-bank cylinder nearest the cabin and 7/8 sit next to the transaxle.
cylinderNumbering.note: GM small-block convention; applying it to the mid-mounted LT6 is an assumption consistent with GM diagnostics (bank 1 = odd). One firing-order site states the viewing direction inconsistently.

bankSequence.note: Derived from the firing order and GM numbering: strictly alternating left-right, one firing every 90 deg of crank rotation.

perBankFiring.note: Each bank behaves like an inline-four firing every 180 deg, so each bank's exhaust gets evenly spaced pulses. A cross-plane V8 gives each bank uneven 90/180/270 deg gaps (the burble).

crankThrows.value: Four throws, each carrying one left and one right rod (1+2, 3+4, 5+6, 7+8). Throws 1 and 4 in phase; throws 2 and 3 at 180 deg. Checked: with a 90-deg V this gives exactly the 1-4-3-8-7-6-5-2 sequence at 90-deg intervals.
crankThrows.note: Derived; GM did not publish throw phasing.

value.formula: rpm / 60 x 4 (whole engine, order 4); per bank rpm / 60 x 2 (order 2)

firingFrequency.note: Per-bank frequency is half the whole-engine value.

torqueCurveFullLoad.basis: crank, SAE J1349 net, US engine
torqueCurveFullLoad.note: Read from GM's 'US LT6 SAE Torque and Power' chart by pixel digitisation of the torque trace; the chart's power trace, recomputed from torque, agrees within 1-2 hp everywhere. Chart starts at about 1,800 rpm and ends at 8,600. Chart peaks read about 1% under the ratings (456 lb-ft vs 460; 666 hp vs 670): multiply by 1.006 to match the ratings within 0.5%. Blue torque trace is hidden behind the power trace near 5,200-5,300 rpm (interpolated).

shapeFeatures.what: dip before the intake resonance step

belowChartEstimate.note: Extrapolated below the chart's 1,800 rpm start; the 1,800-2,500 rpm slope is only about 2.5 Nm per 100 rpm.

wheelDyno.note: Hennessey stock-car chassis dyno, Oct 2023; other stock runs 597-611 whp (Speed Phenom 610 whp / 419 lb-ft). Implies about 90% driveline efficiency on the dyno.

model.value: Tremec TR-9080 8-speed dual-clutch transaxle (GM RPO M1L)

construction.value: two concentric wet clutches (outer: 5 plates, odd gears; inner: 6 plates, even gears), five triple-cone synchronisers, transaxle behind the engine

gearRatios.note: Same set as the Stingray. Cross-checked: 2.91/0.33 = 8.8 spread (SAE article, S10) and the owner's-manual gear speed limits (S18) match these ratios within 3-4%.

finalDrive.note: Stingray: 5.17 with Z51/eLSD, 4.89 base mechanical LSD (S10).

finalDriveBuildUp.value: about 1.566 transfer gear x 3.55 ring and pinion
finalDriveBuildUp.note: Tremec says all versions share a 3.55 ring and pinion and vary the transfer gear; 5.56/3.55 = 1.566. Not confirmed for the Z06. Ring and pinion tooth counts not published (3.55 could be 71/20 or 39/11).

speedAt8600rpm.note: Rear rolling radius 0.345 m. Gears 6-8 are above the drag-limited top speed (top speed is reached in 6th at about 6,850 rpm). In mph: 43, 71, 102, 142, 192.

ownersManualShiftLimits.note: As reported from the 2023 owner's manual (page 202); not seen directly.

rpmAt70mph8th.note: From ratios and 0.345 m rolling radius; about 1,930 rpm in 7th.

shiftTime.note: TR-9080 (Stingray) upshift clutch overlap about 100 ms with no torque interruption. Z06-specific figure not published.

inputTorqueRating.note: Original TR-9080 rating up to 7,500 rpm input; how the Z06 unit was adapted for 8,600 rpm is not published (gap).

efficiency.note: Crank-to-wheel from the stock wheel dyno (600-611 whp vs 670 hp).

differential.value: electronic limited-slip differential (eLSD), standard on every Z06
differential.note: Hydraulically clamped wet multi-plate clutch inside the transaxle (P/E); lock rates not published.

diffModelEstimate.note: Clutch-type approximation for the game, in the prototype's format; eLSDs are fully variable, so tune in testing.

tractionControl.value: Performance Traction Management with several modes, plus launch control

gmDryWeightZ07CarbonWheels.note: 3,434 lb dry, coupe with Z07 and carbon wheels, as copied from GM's sheet; Driven NZ prints 1,561 kg. Corvsport's 2025 guide instead prints 3,500 lb dry (configuration unclear).

curbWeightMeasuredCD_Z07coupe.note: 3,666 lb, Car and Driver, Nov 2022, Z07 coupe.

motorTrendCoupeVsConvertible.note: Coupe 88 lb lighter than the convertible.

curbWeightBaseCoupe.note: No GM curb figure found for the base car. From the C/D Z07 car: plus iron brakes (about +10 kg vs carbon-ceramic), minus Z07 aero (about -5 kg), plus forged aluminium wheels if the test car had carbon wheels (about +19 kg; not known). Range 1,665-1,695 kg.

simulatedMass.note: Base curb 1,680 kg + 75 kg driver, as the prototype does.

weightDistributionFront.note: About 40/60; Motor Authority says 60% over the rear axle; Corvette Magazine says 40/60. Stingray official: 39.4/60.6 (S05). No measured Z06 split found.

comHeight.note: Low mid-engine coupe with dry sump; typical 0.42-0.46 m.

inertiaBox.note: Mass box for yaw inertia, in the prototype's format.

length.note: 184.6 in; Japanese catalogue 4,685 mm. 4,722 mm (185.9 in) with carbon ground effects / Z07 splitter.

width.note: 79.7 in without mirrors; Japanese catalogue 2,025 mm. Stingray 1,933 mm (76.1 in): the Z06 is about 91 mm wider.

groundClearance.note: Not published (gap). Typical for the C8 at the splitter; optional front lift raises the nose roughly 50 mm (A).

frontOverhang.note: Total overhang 4,689 - 2,723 = 1,966 mm split 49/51 front/rear as measured on the side photo.

frontalArea.note: Width x height x 0.84 fill factor (2.024 x 1.234 x 0.84), plus mirrors.

oeTyreZ07.value: Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 R ZP

wheelMaterial.value: forged aluminium standard; optional Carbon Revolution carbon-fibre wheels save 41 lb (18.6 kg) unsprung in total
wheelMaterial.note: Motor Trend: about 10 lb per corner.

wheelTyreInertia.note: Forged aluminium wheel plus tyre; carbon wheels about 10% less.

gripModelBase.note: PS4S road tyre; scaled so the car can reach about 1.10-1.12 g on a skidpad (convertible tests).

gripModelZ07.note: Cup 2 R; tests show 1.16 g on the skidpad (C/D 300 ft, MT 200 ft).

baseSystem.value: Brembo iron discs, 6-piston monobloc front calipers, 4-piston monobloc rear calipers; eBoost electro-hydraulic brake booster

baseDiscFront.note: 14.6 x 1.3 in. Corvsport's 2025 table labels these carbon-ceramic and corvettestory prints wrong mm values; the inch values agree across sources.

baseDiscRear.note: 15.0 x 1.3 in. The rear disc is larger than the front on the base car.

measured_CD_Z07coupe.note: Car and Driver, Nov 2022, carbon-ceramic brakes, Cup 2 R tyres.

measured_MT_Z07coupe.note: Motor Trend, Nov 2022. MT's convertible (Pilot Sport 4S ZP) stopped in about 99 ft by a derived reading.

gameTorqueEstimate.note: Enough to lock the wheels at about 1.3 g with dynamic load transfer (CoM 0.44 m); ABS does the rest.

dragCoefficient.note: Not published (gap). GM only says the Z06 makes 6% more downforce than the C7 ZR1 at 8% less drag (configuration unclear).

dragAreaBase.note: Fitted: 195 mph reached in 6th at about 6,840 rpm (577 hp crank on GM's curve) x 0.90 driveline efficiency, rolling resistance 0.013, air 1.204 kg/m^3, 1,755 kg. Implies Cd about 0.44 on 2.10 m^2 (low confidence).

dragAreaZ07.note: Same fit to 189 mph in 6th (about 6,630 rpm).

downforceBase.note: Standard splitter and spoiler with Gurney/wicker. Motor1 quotes 362 lb for a slightly different wicker/Gurney setup.

downforceZ07.note: Chevrolet figure as reported by Motor Authority, Motor1 and others.

aeroBalanceFront.note: Front/rear split not published; set near the 40/60 weight split.

partsBase.value: front splitter, stall Gurneys under the splitter, rear spoiler with removable wicker

partsZ07.value: larger splitter, front dive planes, underbody strakes, tall pedestal rear wing; stall Gurneys removed

front.value: short/long-arm double wishbone, coil-over, 46 mm monotube dampers
front.note: Coil-over arrangement assumed from the C8 platform (A).

rear.value: short/long-arm double wishbone, coil-over, 46 mm monotube dampers

dampers.value: Magnetic Selective Ride Control 4.0, standard on Z06

z07Chassis.value: FE7 calibration: stiffer springs, retuned magnetic dampers (and bars)

frontLift.value: optional front-axle lift with GPS memory, roughly +50 mm

rideFrequencies.note: Typical for magnetic-damper supercars; tune in testing.

lockToLock.note: Not published (gap). From the turning circle: mean road-wheel lock about 34 deg x 15.7 gives about 3.0 turns at constant ratio; the variable rack quickens off-centre, so about 2.6.

turningCircle.note: 38 ft. Corvsport's metric conversion (11.1 m) is wrong. Stingray: 38 ft, 36.4 ft with Magnetic Ride (S05).

maxRoadWheelAngle.note: From an 11.6 m kerb-to-kerb circle, 2,723 mm wheelbase, 1,684 mm front track.

quarterMile.note: GM preliminary; some listings add 'at 131 mph'.

topSpeedBase.note: 195 mph, Tadge Juechter (Corvette executive chief engineer).

topSpeedZ07.note: 189 mph, Josh Holder (Corvette chief engineer); downforce costs top speed.

zeroTo100kmhExport.note: Listed in the NZ review spec box; low confidence.

nurburgring.note: Cited by Wikipedia from Car and Driver; date and configuration not checked.

magazineTests.note: Numbers via a forum repost of the C/D test box and C/D text syndicated on Yahoo; original page not fetchable.

magazineTests.car: 2023 Z06 coupe, Z07 package, carbon wheels
magazineTests.note: Then a record for MT. Coupe ran about 0.2 s slower and 3.4 mph slower through the quarter than MT's Pilot Sport 4S convertible (more drag). MT 0-60 and quarter-mile times not obtained (gap).

magazineTests.outlet: Car and Driver (as cited by Corvsport)

sound.summary: Flat-plane crank: each bank fires every 180 deg (an inline-four's even pulse train), banks alternate every 90 deg, so the exhaust is a clean high-pitched shriek with little low-order burble. Dominant pitch is firing frequency (order 4): 60 Hz at a 900 rpm idle, 300 Hz at 4,500 rpm, 573 Hz at the 8,600 rpm limiter. Strong induction sound from twin 87 mm throttle bodies right behind the cabin.

exhaustHeaders.value: stainless steel 4-2-1 headers per bank, chosen with the flat-plane layout for high-rpm scavenging

headerPairingEstimate.value: left bank: primaries 1+7 and 3+5 merge; right bank: 2+8 and 4+6 merge (cylinders 360 deg apart share a secondary), so each secondary gets one pulse per revolution and each bank's collector one every 180 deg
headerPairingEstimate.note: Standard 4-2-1 practice for a 1-2-4-3 bank firing pattern; GM did not publish the pairing.

bankCollection.value: Banks stay separate through their own 4-2-1 collectors. Whether the two banks join (X- or H-pipe) before the mufflers is not published.
bankCollection.note: Aftermarket cat-back systems advertise adding an X-pipe to tie the banks together, which suggests the factory system does not have one (unconfirmed).

catalysts.value: not published; assumed one catalyst per bank downstream of the header collectors

mufflersAndValves.value: valved active exhaust; the exhaust valves move in 2-degree steps rather than open/shut, giving four sound modes: Weather (quietest), Tour, Sport, Track (all valves open). Intake manifold valves also change the sound.
mufflersAndValves.note: From Chevrolet's 'Corvette Academy' video as reported by Motor1.

tips.value: centre exit, four round tips in a single horizontal row inside one bezel in the rear diffuser
tips.note: Layout read from a CC BY 2.0 rear photo. Chevrolet says the bezels are shaped to reflect sound up toward the cockpit; The Drive mentions reverse-trumpet shapes to raise cabin exhaust noise. Motor1 says the tips are not offered outside the US (unclear).

intakeSound.value: Twin 87 mm throttle bodies feed the split plenum directly behind the cabin; reviewers single out the induction noise.

interiorFullThrottle_CD_coupe.note: Car and Driver, Nov 2022: the targa coupe measured 94 dBA at wide-open throttle.

interiorIdle.note: C/D idle figure not obtained (gap). Estimate 55-62 dBA for a loud valved V8 behind the seats.

interior70mph.note: C/D 70-mph figure not obtained (gap). Estimate 72 dBA on Pilot Sport 4S, 75 dBA on Cup 2 R (C/D's long-term car notes heavy Cup 2 R road noise).

ownerMeasuredStock.note: Owner post on Corvette Club UK; method and distance unknown; low confidence.

stationaryPassByStandard.note: No published stationary or pass-by test found (gap).

limiterBehaviour.value: Hard fuel cut at 8,600 rpm. At full throttle the gearbox completes upshifts at about 8,500 rpm, so in automatic mode the limiter is rarely heard; in manual mode expect a fast fuel-cut bounce of about 150 rpm.
limiterBehaviour.note: The 8,600 fuel cut and 8,500 shift point are reported (P); the bounce character is an estimate.

overrunCharacter.value: Rev-matched blips on every downshift ('Whumm, whumm, whumm!!!' - Motor Authority). Pops and crackles on lift-off are not described by any source; expect a clean, light crackle at most in Sport/Track.
overrunCharacter.note: Gap: no source documents overrun crackle.

shiftSound.value: DCT upshifts with about 100 ms overlap, no torque gap; a brief note dip rather than a gunshot ignition cut

freelyLicensedRecordings.licenceNotes: CC BY needs attribution (author, title, licence, link). CC BY-SA also requires anything made from it to be shared under BY-SA, which is awkward inside a Roblox game; use it as a listening reference only. 'Licence review pending' means Commons has not yet confirmed the YouTube CC licence. Commons notes YouTube's CC licence changed from 3.0 to 4.0 on 1 Aug 2025, not retroactively. bodyStyle.value: two-seat mid-engine coupe with removable roof panel; cab-forward cockpit, long rear deck over the engine

z06Differences.value: rear fenders and body about 91 mm wider than the Stingray; deeper front fascia with larger intakes; larger side intakes beginning in the door; centre quad exhaust; ducktail spoiler (base) or tall pedestal wing (Z07)

photosUsed.what: white Z06 with the roof open, side profile (cross-check; file title says coupe)
photosUsed.author: Charles from Port Chester, New York

photosUsed.what: orange Z06 with Z07 wing, rear three-quarter (exhaust tips)
photosUsed.author: John Bauld

visualBlockout.method: Side photo measured in pixels; scale from the 2,723 mm wheelbase between wheel centres; overhangs scaled to the published 4,689 mm length because the photo's perspective shrinks the ends. Accuracy about +-3-5% of length.

heights.note: Roof peak is the published height; others from the photo (+-5%) except the splitter lip (typical value) and the Z07 wing (estimated).

value.nose: low, sharp wedge with a pointed centre; wide splitter; Z06 fascia has large outboard intakes; short bonnet rising steeply to the cowl
value.cabin: cab-forward; steeply raked windscreen; short flat roof; flying-buttress sail panels running back to the deck
value.rear: small upright rear window between the buttresses over the engine; long, nearly flat engine deck; high, square-cut tail with thin horizontal lamps and an integrated ducktail; big diffuser with centre quad tips
value.sides: deep scoop from the door into a large side intake ahead of the rear wheel; strong rear haunches

tyres.value: Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 R ZP, same sizes

brakes.value: carbon-ceramic, 398 x 38 mm front, 390 x 34 mm rear

aero.value: 734 lb (3,265 N) at 186 mph; larger splitter, dive planes, strakes, pedestal wing

wheels.value: often fitted with carbon-fibre wheels (about -10 lb per corner)

massDelta.note: +88 lb vs coupe (MT); C/D cars differed by 133 lb but with different equipment.

torque.note: at 6,300 rpm; Japanese catalogue says 623 Nm

suggestedTargets.note: 0-100 km/h is about 0.15-0.2 s more than 0-60 mph (2.6 s); keep 314 km/h for the base car.

topSpeedGear.value: 6th at about 6,850 rpm (drag-limited); 5th runs out at about 310 km/h at 8,600

gaps: GM press kit and media.gm.com spec pages returned HTTP 403; GM figures were taken from Wikipedia and spec-site copies of GM's sheet (some with copy errors, noted).
Car and Driver interior sound at idle and at a 70-mph cruise not obtained (only full throttle: 94 dBA coupe, 96 convertible). Estimates given.
No exterior, stationary or pass-by dB figure from a reliable source; one owner measurement only.
Drag coefficient and frontal area not published; CdA fitted to top speed (0.92 base, 0.99 Z07) - low confidence, it absorbs driveline-loss and air-density errors.
No GM curb weight for the base Z06 coupe; only GM dry weight (Z07 + carbon wheels) and C/D's measured Z07 coupe. Measured weight distribution for the Z06 not found (40/60 approximate).
Ground clearance, ride height and front-lift height not published.
Steering lock-to-lock turns not published; estimated 2.6.
Exhaust details not published: catalyst count and position, whether the banks cross over, muffler internals, header primary lengths and pairing.
